analysis:
Examined both primary analyses and all replayed metadata, documentation and patches. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md:377 (head) changes retirement coordination from whole-batch locking to 16-file slices, releasing the removal lock and epoch barrier between slices, rechecking ownership and stopping on refusal. changelog.d/ssd-retirement-in-slices.md:3–9 reports reduced lookup/publication blocking and longer background sweeps; this is a measurement, not a latency guarantee. No independently supported security regression follows from these documentation changes.
The reported SSDPrefixCache.swift change at head 1794–1800 introduces interleaving between slices and is consistent with the documentation, but its source was omitted from this integration replay; the prior analysis alone cannot verify it. Relevant contracts are T-041/A-001/TB-007 cache isolation, authenticated storage and retention, plus A-018 availability. Supplied patches do not change TTL, scope derivation, HMAC naming, encryption, KEK purge, attestation, authorization, billing or privileged authority.
Material uncertainty remains in the new retirement implementation and its callers: SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices, SSDCacheEpochStore.performOwnedRetirement, SSDDiskBudget.retireActiveEntries and SSDPrefixCache.performIndexedRemoval. Further review must verify per-slice durable epoch/binding validation, termination on ownership refusal, nonwaiting file leases, protection against deleting newly published replacements, and consistent unlink/index/byte accounting and reconciliation across interleaved writes or root changes. These are PR-specific unresolved contracts, not observed missing controls. Replay is incomplete (four source units omitted), and no implementation evidence resolves these questions here.
